review_summary: The beginning of a beautiful friendship
review_text: I love this skirt and have gotten so many compliments on it. Ive been looking for a nice long skirt to wear to work when Im sick of pants, and Im pleased to see that this garment can easily be dressed down for the weekend as well. Like other reviewers said, it came to me wrinkled (what can you do?), but it steamed flat really easily. I love the pockets and the way the skirt moves when I walk. Im super short, so luckily I didnt expect this to hit me right at the knee. In reality it hits me about midcalf (which is exactly what I was looking for). It seems like it would be easy to hem if I didnt like the length, though, which might be good news for other shorties who really do want a kneelength skirt.My only real gripe is the zipper. Invisible zippers are always a pain, and this was no different, especially because the top has no hook and eye. Maybe I just got lucky with my zipper, but at first it got so stuck that I thought the whole thing might be too small for me (in reality its actually a tiny bit big). Maybe it will get easier after a few more wears, but for now its pretty annoying. Im grateful for the elastic back of the skirt because I think it would be too big on me without the slight cinching it provides. Still, I like a little breathing room in my clothes, so its nice to know that if I eat a big lunch I wont explode out of it. Definitely seems like theres some room for minor weight fluctuations in this skirt.Sorry about this being The Worst Photo Ever, but I find the user pictures super helpful, so I want prospective buyers to have mine too. :)

review_text: I was so excited when I saw this coat go on sale as I couldnt justify the original $140 cost. I went with a small, and it fits very well, though it is a little bit looser around the waist than I had expected. It is a beautiful coat, and I was very happy with it at first. However, only a few days after I bought it, the hook that is used to hang the coat broke. Its not a normal cloth hook and is made out of a small chain, so Im not really surprised that it broke so quickly as the coat is heavy. A few days later, one of the buttons attaching the knit part of the collar popped off (must have come off during the day because I was unable to find it). The coat did not come with any extra buttons so the collar is currently not attached on one side until I can find a similar button. Finally, after only having this coat for about a month, the insides of the pockets have begun to develop holes. The material the pockets are made of is very thin, and again, Im not terribly surprised. The inner lining of the coat is made of the same material and has also torn in several places. Overall I am a bit disappointed in this coat. It looks very nice and is comfortable, but seems to be very cheaply made. I would have expected a $100 coat to hold up better. I was hoping to have this coat for years to come, but based on the amount of wear and tear it was already begun to show after just a few weeks, I doubt that will be likely. Its a shame, it really is a unique and beautiful coat.

The good: these pants are the right length and fit me (which is hard to do). the bad: the pants gape between the top two buttons. the WORST: the pants smell horrible. A mix betwen bad laundry and acid. I was gonig to return these because of the smell but pants are hard to find for my figure so i decided to roll the dice and wash them to see if I could get rid of the smell. Not only did the smell not go away, it made the entire laundry load (which thankfully was just night clothes) stink horribly as well. I used baking soda and white vinegar to try to get rid of the smell (it cleaned up the other clothes but somehow not the jeans) and then i used industrial cleaner on the jeans and they are in the washer now. Lets hope that works because i wont be getting my money ($66 dollars worth) back because I chose to try to get the smell out. DO NOT BE FOOLED. I would say this was just a really bad pair of jeans and this isnt normal but I have ordered a similar pair of Karaoke Songstress Jeans from this site before and it was equally bad but i decided to return them becaues they were too small as well. Modcloth has definitely gone down in quality recently.

I figured since the two tops are the exact same style, they would fit exactly the same.  I pulled the tags off both tops and hung them in my closet.  Wrong. The sleeves on my navy top are so tight that I can barely wear it.  I can wear it with a loose cardigan to hide the appearance of the sleeve around my arm and to also hide the fact that the arm pit of the sleeve stops about 2 inches from my armpit because it simply wont go up any higher; there is no give on the fabric.  I cant return it since I took the tags off of it.  And its not like its a low priced item, so there goes that money down the tube.  Im just super disappointed with the way it fits.  It fits great everywhere else and looks amazing with my height, but the sleeves make it unwearable. For an XL, it should fit. I do not have ginormous arms of a weightlifter.

review_summary: I love this coat!! It jus
review_text: I love this coat!! It just arrived this morning and I couldnt be happier about it! The style is very classic, so I cant ever see it going out of style. Its made of heavy, thick material and the seams are all neat and well done. I read a review saying that the diagonal zip looked strange, but I think it really adds to the design and helps make the coat appear more slimming. I wasnt too sure about the collar after having read a number of reviews about people removing the ribbed bit, but I love the way it looks both on and off. I was slightly apprehensive about the sizing of this coat, as I have large hips and Ive noticed that normally coats on me are very tight across the hips and far too baggy around the waist. I was so happy to see that the zip of this doesnt actually start at the bottom of the coat, it starts 25cm (9inches) from the bottom, which means that it doesnt pull around you and give you an odd shape (it also makes it much easier to sit in.) As I live in Australia I got the large (which is quite fitted on me) because I wont have the need of wearing anything bulky underneath to keep me warm. If you do live in a colder climate, I would definitely consider sizing up, just so you can fit jumpers underneath. The coat does run true to size though.

Here are the flat measurements from a 2X to help you. The bust is 23 inches flat (46) PLEASE see more specific as this dress bust is not the whole story, the arm hole is 12.5 inches and the measurement right above the buttons is 21 inches (42). My thoughts The material is thick. The color is a bitter darker than the color in the model pictures. It is lined. Wished this one had pockets. The bust was my biggest problem. My measurement from my back to across the front of my bust is 47 inches. That said, I wear a 38B or 40B if I can find them. The flat measurement for this dress is 46, BUT the bust of this dress does NOT include the bust part that sticks out, the tailored darts for the bust. Though I always love this detail, not on this dress for me. If you lay the dress flat and keep it flat, there is room where your chest would fill the extra material. Its about 5 inches bigger! What does that mean? Small busted girls, this is not for you. Think those old pointed bras and put that room in the bust on this dress. There isnt much stretch at the bust, but there is the whole area you need to fill. You can see that the second model with short hair doesnt fill out the dress as well as the top model pictures. It doesnt fit like the top model if you are small busted. So, endowed girls... rock this dress. Small chested, pass. Returning this one, but if it fit it would have been a great purchase.

Like other reviews, there is an awesome elastic band in the back to give a slight stretch for a snug fit and a zipper that is kind of hidden behind a pocket (Love the pockets!) for easier slipping into the skirt. The material is relatively thin, not see through thin, and there is a blue silk like slip underneath that layer which really adds to the quality, Definitely a must have skirt that can become a classic that I will wear for several years (only time will tell). My other issue was that the main zipper of the jacket seems a little cheap  it didnt zip up and down super easily and got caught sometimes. review_summary: First off, I need to say
review_text: First off, I need to say that randomly posting that an article of clothing fits wrong! without offering your measurements and the size of the item you bought is, to quote Jack Sparrow, maddeningly unhelpful, and I wish you wouldnt. Okay, as for this hooded sweater... It is very heavyweight. I dont find the hood to be flimsy, its the same as any other hooded sweater, but compared to the thickness of the sweater itself, it may seem thin. The shirt did not come to me with an odd smell or anything of the sort, thankfully. It isnt as long as I thought, but its about the same as every other hoodie Ive bought. To me, the medium fits like a medium, so you have to just try it, I guess.  I have somewhat long arms, and the sleeves hit at the wrist. In the pictures, Im wearing size 4 LEVIS that are midlength, and the hoodie sits about halfway over my belt loops, just for length and size reference.  I agree with all the others who say the hardware is cheap  I havent had anything fall off yet, but so far Im treating it with kid gloves because I can see how the snaps are simply shoved through the fabric. The zipper is metal and does seem a bit sticky, so Im being careful with it.  The cuffs are not at all too tight for me, so I havent needed to snap or unsnap anything.  I like the metal detailing, and I think its possible that the hoodie could be used as a layering piece, but for me it is already very warm.

I thought about keeping it, folding the hood over, and sewing on new buttons... but I think for the price, I should love everything about it. I would love to see more coats of this style, with a big hood, though!!

review_summary: In my opinion, the only t
review_text: In my opinion, the only thing that makes these jeans truly special is that they are made in the US. I saw that some reviewers were quite upset about that, but theyre not so thin theyre leggings, just the same as any other stretch jeans.I was worried the waist would be tight on me, but if anything its a little loose. These would be worth the price to me if the people who made them were paid well for their time. I asked the experts via the mod chat and they knew nothing more than that they are made in USA, which is a good start. I contacted the manufacturer to learn more, but they have not responded to me and its been nearly a week.The high waist doesnt magically change my shape like I sort of expected it to based on the other reviews, but its comfortable. I wear a sturdy leather belt with all jeans, but it looks a little bulky up at my waist. For now Im going beltless or trying them out with a skinnier belt I would normally wear with a dress. I will hem these soon, but thats actually easier to do on this thinner material than thick denim jeans.

It has just started getting chilly here (mid 30slow 40s) and even when Im wearing this over another jacket or sweater, Im still cold. I knew this wasnt supposed to be the warmest coat according to Modcloths rating system, but this is worse than I expected. Ill have to do some heavy layering under this, and Im really disappointed that I spent so much on a coat that wont get me through the Northwests mild winters. It looks heavy and warm, but really really isnt. But the look and fit are so great, it is honestly the most attractive coat Ive tried on that fits me in years. The only other bad thing I can say about it is the pocket placement is odd. The pockets are way towards the front of the coat, so when you put your hands in them you have to hunch your shoulders forward. But aside from awkward pocket placement and lack of warmth, its a very nice coat. Since finding a good fit is so hard for me, perhaps I cant be too picky.

I ordered this dress for my schools prom on May 9th. I started off with a blue, straight, strapless gown from Windsor, which was lovely, but I felt straps needed to be added. I had resigned to thinking that I would go to a tailor to get straps professionally added when I came across this beautiful gown while browsing Modcloth. I knew that this gown would be perfect for me! It arrived slightly wrinkled, but that is expected when things are shipped in small boxes. Nothing a little trip to the dry cleaners cant fix! When I put this dress on, I instantly felt like a princess. The skirt is the perfect volume, not to flat, not too poofy, and it swirls around beautifully when I walk. I feel like I just walked into the ballroom of the Titanic! I was initially concerned about the ankle length skirt, thinking it would be more tea length than I wanted, but it is PERFECT! It ends right at my ankle so it can show off my shoes and I dont have to worry about dragging the hem through any puddles. I usually wear between a 6 and 8 in US sizing, so I went for a UK 12 because I would rather have the dress be slightly big than too small. After my tailor messed up the original dress I ordered I was in a panic.  I was on a tight budget and didnt want to spend much more money on a dress than I already had. I remembered that ModCloth had plus size dresses at reasonable prices. I fell in love with this dress and ordered it.  It came quickly. It was beautifully packaged and took my breath away when I opened it.  I felt wonderful in it much better than my original dress.  I am sad to see that some reviewers felt the fabric was cheap.  I thought it was beautifully made, the fabric had a lovely sheen and of course the lace was amazing. The new tailors did a great job getting it ready in about 2 weeks. All in all I feel like the money I wasted was on the original dress (which was a knock off from overseasactually not a horror story until I took it to the tailor!). Anyway, if you are on a budget, love lace and want to feel bridal on your special day, I dont think you can go wrong with this. I added a belt which doesnt show in the long picture but I missed the bling on the original dress.  I also used a 1 hoop slip as the fabric is a bit sheer and I loved the way the lace looked when it was able to float a bit. Now that its on sale, dont be shy.  Its lovely!

The XL mostly fit OK but was definitely too large up top. I was going to meet with a seamstress about alterations, but in the meantime the Large came back in stock so I ordered that and its a perfect fit! Now I have to not gain any weight in the next year, but thats a good motivation :). As others have mentioned, the quality is great and I just love the classic styling. Its very comfortable. It has a side zip so you dont have to unbutton all the back buttons to get into it. The bodice/bust is structured on the inside and slightly padded, kind of like a bathing suit. Wasnt sure how easily this could be altered if necessary, but its probably doable. If you are inbetween sizes and smaller on the bust, go for the smaller size. And dont despair if the size you want is out of stock  sign up for an alert and keep checking, as it looks like they keep restocking. Customer service has also been GREAT through this whole process. Im so thrilled to have found a lovely dress within my budget and to have escaped the bridal boutique experience! I also decided to take a credit for the return of the XL so I can splurge on more Modcloth goodies.

I do find that the top is quite large, which can be attended to somewhat by cinching the straps as tight as they will go. For me, the straps are my least favourite part of the dress (and why I giving it only 4 stars) and I may look into replacing them entirely with something thicker and more mature. I will also need to wear a camisole underneath for work, but paired with any number of the Cream of the Crop cardigans that Modcloth sells, this dress is a great addition to the work wardrobe. Or, you could throw on some heals and wear it for an evening out. I personally would not wear it as a sun dress, as the heavy black skirt would make it too hot, but I love that you can match it with literally any colour of accessories and basically have a whole new look. At the sale price, this was an excellent buy.

The magnets that are supposed to hold the inner layer of the front in place dont work very well.

review_summary: I love this coat. Got it
review_text: I love this coat. Got it 2 winters ago when I needed a new winter coat. Still in love with it. Still bring it out when the temp drops. The only downfall for me is the coat raises drastically whenever I raise or lift my arms.Its roomy enough for me to layer underneath and it doesnt look big or chunky. Nicely made. I love the metal part of the coat that you use to hang it on hooks, so cute. And I like the collar, its a great and fun feature to get different looks with.Its been dry cleaned a few times and worn for 2 winters, going on its 3rd. Still holding up great. Those pockets can hold a lot. Ill shove my gloves and winter scarf in there when I dont need them and they fit.I like winter coats that cover my butt (more warmth!) but being very short, most winter coats swallow me up and I look ridiculous and shorter than my 4 10. I dont know, I think it might be the cut but this coat doesnt make me looks shorter than I am. The arms are a bit long for me, but if I fold the sleeves back, theyre perfect and it also add more character to the coat.Just get used to zipping it up, the zipper doesnt go straight up and down the middle of your body like many zippers do. It goes up and down at a diagonal.I love this coat. If you get it, I hope you love it too.

review_summary: Give me a moment, Im get
review_text: Give me a moment, Im getting emotional... okay. I havent been comfortable leaving my house in shorts for years  YEARS. Despite being a huge fan of the body positivity movement, Im very selfconscious about my legs and tummy sometimes, and Im almost always wearing pants of some sort. These shorts literally changed everything. Even though I still wear leggings or tights underneath them usually, I will jump at every opportunity I get to wear these out  Im wearing them right now! The waist hits right at my natural waist right under my belly button, the leg openings are comfy and not tight at all on my thighs, and even if theyre short, they make me look and feel like a pinup. So magical are these shorts that Ive actually purchased a few CROP TOPS and plan to wear them this summer. (That is REVOLUTIONARY for me.) Ive also begun tucking all my shirts into them because of how cute it looks, and nothing serves as a better base for a great outfit than a good bodysuit and these shorts. WARNING: If you get these, follow the care instructions and do NOT tumbledry them! My dad threw them in the dryer with a bunch of other jeans and the hem dried up all crumply and mangled, and I actually cried because I thought they were ruined. A good soak of the hems in cool water, some careful adjusting, a vigorous press with a large book, and a few hours of laying flat to dry, and they were good as new. Dont make my laundry mistakes  but DEFINITELY buy these shorts.

(This came to nearly 80$ when shipping and boarder fees were added.) While I do normally wear a large size these days, despite the pleasant stretch of the material and the aid of shape wear, it will be a while before I will be fitting myself into this dress without looking pregnant. The fabric itself is soft to the touch, though it is not as thick/structured as I had assumed from the other descriptions. The colour is beautiful, though I did also have to go around snipping little seam ends off from sleeves, hems, etc, as there were 12 threads sort of dangling off of random places. Lastly, even just in wearing this around my house to see what I could get away with, I noticed that the back slit tends to ride up. Perhaps this is because I carry my weight around my middle, or perhaps this is because I have a shorter torso and longer legs  but as a teacher, Id be weary wearing this in front of children, as, a two room walk away, I realized that the stop of the slit was sitting at the very bottom of my rear. In terms of length though, the dress stops right above my knee. The overall silhouette would be very attractive, were it not for the expansion of the ruching across my apparently broad midsection!

Fit:Finding tops and dresses for my 38H chest without looking like a bag everywhere is kind of tough.  This dress worked out pretty well for me, so I actually bought three colors (my reviews for the three will be the same, until the color blurb at the end).The 2x size had enough room in the bust that the waist sits very comfortably in a sort of empirestyle way.  The waist is a little bigger than my ribcage and natural waist, so I may take it in a few inches eventually so that it will fit lower on my torso.The hem hits right in the center of my knees.Cut/quality:The cut is pretty flattering on my bust.  The neckline doesnt expose my cleavage, and the ruching on the bust and the waist sort of balance the whole thing out by lending a bit of flare to the skirt as well.  The top is lined with the same fabric, the skirt is unlined.  The instructions say to handwash and flat dry, however, Ive washed these in my undergarment bag on cold/delicate cycle, and hung it up to dry: it held up just fine.Out and about:This dress is simple enough that its great for dressing up and wearing casually! It looks good with scarves and button down cardigans, and its fun to pair with colored tights. Color:Its hard to describe the color of this dress.  It is much more of a saturated purple in person than the darker plum pictured.  Its still very pretty, and looks great with rustycolored accessories.

Im about 57.5, 150 lbs.First, the good: These jeans are SUPER comfy, and they hug my bum nicely. The fabric is nicely stretchy and forgiving. I definitely think Ill be getting a lot of use out of them. However, there are definitely some drawbacks that I wanted to share.I originally ordered an 11. When they arrived, the fit was the very snug, skinny jeans with a retro flair sort that I wanted. The length was perfect. However, the buttons on the fly had gaps/bulges even when I was standing up, so I exchanged for a 13. The 13 fits more like a traditional slim fit than a skinny jean. Theyre quite a bit longer, so Ill probably be cuffing them most of the time. The thing that bothers me the most, though, is that I still get a sizable button gap between the second and third button. I feel like this is a flaw in the design rather than a sizing issue  The fabric is on the thinner side because its stretchy, and I think the bottom three buttons would be better off as false buttons over a zipper fly. The buttons also are a bit more on the cheap side  I have $20 jeans with heftier buttons. I also agree with the comments about the waistband needing to be stiffer  It does roll anytime I sit. Also, I would have preferred that the denim on the pockets extend a bit further in, as I have to check my pockets to see if theyre untucked anytime I stand up.Overall, good jeans, but for $60, I would have expected better quality.

This was my first purchase from ModCloth, so I wasnt entirely sure what to expect. I had had my eye on this for quite some time, so when it came back in stock, I decided to buy it. After reading the other buyers reviews, I was a little bit wary about the possible length problem, since I am over 59 and very skinny. My biggest issue with most clothing is the length (including sleeve length, since I have long arms). It is hard for me to find clothing that is long enough AND slim enough. To be on the safe side, I purchased a large, figuring I could always take it in if it were too wide. Luckily, I didnt have to. When the hoodie came today, I was excited and curious to see how it fit and looked. As soon as I took it out of the package, I was in love. The material was nice, and it was so gosh darn cute! When I put it on, it fit me perfectly, resting halfway down my hips. The sleeves were long enough, coming a couple of inches down my hand. It was slim enough to look attractive, even on my tiny frame, yet loose enough to be comfortable. My advice for anyone looking to buy this  SIZE UP. If a large can fit a string bean like me, then sizing up should be no problem for anyone else. Appearancewise, this is now one of my favorite articles of clothing. Its edgy and unique, quite different than a lot of jackets you see in the store. I wore it with a pair of red skinny jeans and a gray tee shirt. Definitely wellworth the price.

This is a fabulous dress! I hemmed and hawed between buying in blue or purple, but picked up the red and purple during the Thanksgiving sale. Fabric is nice and heavy, drapes well but is also breathable. I got one with gold buttons and it looks fantastic. As far as fit goes, I have a weird body and was pleased it worked on me, it emphasizes my large bust but not in a bad way, and since Im not very hippy the pockets dont make me look larger. I was also pleased to find out that for once with a ModCloth dress, I wasnt stuffing my chest into a size L. I was accidentally sent the red in a S so I had the chance to compare the size range, and if you are trying to decide between a M and L, I easily could have fit my small bottom end and my chest a little less comfortably  into a M. I have two caveats for this dress: one, the cut emphasizes a belly on short/shorter waisted people, so unless you have a rack of doom to balance out your belly like I do, it may not look very flattering. The other note is about the buttons and fabric...one star came off this dress because the buttons are hollow and I cant stand how cheap they sound (the black/silver buttons on other Coach Tour dresses are much nicer) and because the fabric rubbed magenta off all over my white leather phone case when I put it in the pockets, but I dont remember any warnings about dye transfers with this product so beware! Otherwise, fantastic purchase and I cant wait to get my other one in the correct size!

I did not hate it at first, but my boyfriend (who thinks I am the hottest thing in the world) kinda gave an eh response.  Said it was too poofy for the shortness of it and looked like a costume (and for reference, he never complains about my clothing being too short).  At first I was not sure I agreed, but when I put on some pumps with it, I felt that I looked like a doll... and not in a good way.  The skirt did arrive wrinkled and the pleats had to be fussed with.  Perhaps if I were to fuss some more I could have brought some of the poof down, but I really dont want to spend that much time fussing with my clothes, so I am returning it.  If you are built like me (long legs / wide hips) you may want to be cautious with this one.  If you are built differently, it may look great on you!  For size reference, in dresses I generally wear a 6, sometimes a 4.  For Modcloth, I am either a small or medium depending on the item. review_summary: Taking it out of the plas

I was wary as I live in Australia and the cost of returns would be phenomenal if I got the sizing wrong. For all the other Australian ladies, my measurements are h 163cm, bra 12C, waist 73cm, hips ~100cm (usually fit in a size 10 or 12). According to the ModCloth guide Im on the lower end of the L and after reading that the fabric of this dress is stretchy, I decided to get the M. It fits perfectly! Great length too, it sits a little above my knee. Perhaps a little short for work but I wore it anyway and the first time I did a colleague fell in love with it too and interrogated me as to where I got it from! (I was happy to tell her of course!) I have a long torso and short legs but that doesnt seem to matter with this dress. Also, the fact that it has pockets was an instant win for me as I like to have my train ticket and phone within easy reach when commuting to work. The material is, as many others have said, not too thick or thin, so it can be worn in summer (even here in Brisbane) and I look forward to wearing it in winter too with a long sleeve top underneath, tights and knee high boots. I was really excited about this jacket and thought that the only thing that could possibly be bad about it was maybe the fit I was wrong. As soon as I pulled it out of the box, I said what the heck is that?! Because it didnt look anything like the pictures. The faux leather has an oddly metallic sheen; its more of a gun metal gray than a black (see picture). I was pretty disappointed by this, but thought maybe I was overreacting and tried it on anyway. The fit was a little tight, but overall okay and not too uncomfortable. But after I put it on, I really looked at it and realized the the zipout hoodie layer is the most bizarre thing. Its not just a hoodie that you can take out and its not a hood that you can zip off its a 2inch wide stretch of hoodie material the runs the length of the jacket with a second zipper to make it look like youre wearing a hoodie underneath. Essentially the only point of it is for looks, not for warmth or versatility or anything useful. Which would be one thing. Except that the bottom like 6inches of the sleeves are hoodie material and they dont zip off. Which means you can zip off the extra strip of hoodie fabric to get rid of the second zipper (and why should I have to doublezipper a single jacket?), but you will be left with these confusing sleeves that make it look sort of like youre wearing two jackets when youre very obviously not.Overall, really disappointing and confusing. This could have been a really nice jacket, but it feels to me like they cheaped out.

Ive been looking for a cute, flattering, nonblack/nonbeige winter coat for a while, and Im so happy I found one. I am typically a 2x/3x and the options for nondowdy winter coats are pretty slim in that size range. I ordered this in a 3x and it is just a tad too large, but that is what I prefer with my winter coats to accommodate bulky sweaters underneath. This coat is a lighter weight winter coat, just perfect for mild Seattle winters. The gray fabric is a bit darker than it appears in the pictures, but the multicolored flecks are still apparent and liven up the fabric nicely. I thought I might want a tailor to add an interior zipper or some buttons to help keep the coat closed, but surprisingly the toggles do that just fine for me. The flared shape and defined waistline are very flattering and overall the coat is simply adorable. My only minor gripe is that the sleeves are a touch too short, but I am 510 with unusually long arms and have never found a winter coat with long enough sleeves. Ill be wearing this coat until it falls apart.

review_summary: WOW. When I first got eng
review_text: WOW. When I first got engaged, this dress didnt exist, and none of Modcloths other dresses felt quite right for my small summer backyard beach wedding. I wanted a simple Aline lace dress without bling or showy details, not too revealing, with an interesting back. Easy, right? Nope. I looked everywhere; bigbox, scary boutiques, other online shops. I even ordered a custom dress from Etsy for 2x the cost, which I still had to alter (and it ended up butchered). With 3 weeks left, I was panicking. Luckily I checked here again and even with no reviews, I ordered this. When I finally opened the box my heart skipped a beat. It is SO gorgeous in person. The texture/quality of the fabric and detail are so richlooking, yet understated. I am between sizes XS/S and chose the larger. This was bad because I have a small bust and it was way too big up top. If you are bustier, order your usual. It?s also very long but works with 3.54inch heels for shorties like me. Even with an odd fit, I got goosebumps. Ended up quick exchanging for XS, which was great in the bust, but it needed to be let out 1? at the waist by a talented seamstress to fully zip (no stretch). Dress was perfect (July+FL=HOT). Bottom is seethrough in light, so wear nude underthings (best part  regular bra!) or a long slip. I added a simple satin sash for another dimension. This dress is so much better than anything else I tried on. Everyone was shocked at how beautiful it is and how little I paid. Thank you, Modcloth!

review_summary: I am a plussized gal at 5
review_text: I am a plussized gal at 56 and about 210 pounds. Based on my measurements, I ordered Size 1x, and it fits PERFECTLY. The thinness makes it a little prone to wrinkling, but nothing horrendous, and certainly not as easytowrinkle as a fabric such as linen. I suspect that the selfbelt will never tie as beautifully as it does in the photo, but I swapped it out with my own belt to make it a little more me.The color is a mustard/goldenrod, not a bright yellow. The length is perfect for me  just to my knees. For me, the location of the belt loops was perfect  right on my ribcage, just below where an empire waist would be, but above my natural waist. But this would vary from person to person.As a larger gal, I often have trouble with the fit of items in the bust and shoulders, and the tightness of sleeves around my arms. I had no trouble at all with this dress in any of these areas. The bust doesnt gape, the shoulders dont pull, and the sleeves are cute large enough to accommodate larger arms (at least in the 1x size).I am planning on buying more of this dress in other colors!

review_summary: I love these jeans! I hav
review_text: I love these jeans! I have been searching for a great pair of jeans for what feels like forever, and I have finally some that prove that they do exist for people with my shape. I carry a lot of weight in my stomach and have fairly muscular thighs and calves, so jeans would always be too tight around my stomach while fitting my legs, or way too big on my legs while fitting my stomach, and skinny jeans were just straight out due to the size of my calves. These jeans fit me PERFECTLY. They are comfortable without being too casual, and they are very flattering. I will be ordering a pair in every color! I did follow the advice of other customers and went up a size (I am normally an 18 so I went up to 2X) and they are pretty perfect. The length is a bit long but it doesnt look bad to leave them be or to cuff them. The only issue Ive really had is that even after a couple of washes, the dye is still rubbing off on my fingers, so be careful about what you wear with them for the first few wears or just wash them a few times before you put them on. Overall these jeans are fantastic and I couldnt be happier! Thank you for making me feel great about myself!

review_text: I adore this dress!  I wore it to an October wedding in Virginia, and it was perfect. I have NEVER gotten so many compliments from strangers. Also, the fabric is stretchy, so if youre like me and dont fall uniformly into one size, it might still fit.  The way that the lace is positioned made me look supersexy and curvy, but with the high neck and kneeish length, it still felt appropriate for a church and country club.  It was comfortable to move in (b/c of the stretchiness).  My only (minor) complaint is that I wouldve liked the lace to go all the way around, but as another reviewer mentioned, its pretty reasonably priced, so thats a small sacrifice.  Overall, I am so so happy with this dress.  Cant wait to wear it again!  P.S.  I accessorized with a nude/tan clutch, nude/tan wedges, and a nude/tan linen wrap, and that seemed to work well.  I also opted for an updo so that I wouldnt cover up any of the beautiful lace. :)

Additionally, it fits perfectly true to size, looks awesome in the dark, and garnered me compliments from pretty much everyone who saw me whilst I was wearing it, including 3 different ladies I subsequently referred to Mod Cloth because they wanted to purchase it for themselves! My only complaint (like many of the other reviewers) is the collar: it looks out of place, wrinkles easily, and doesnt lay flat. review_summary: Zipper takes PATIENCE; Pocket openings curl out, require sew
review_text: I recently ordered this in green (on sale) and returned it, and then ordered it in black (not on sale but with a coupon) so I will discuss both here.BLACK: This is a lot of money for what it is: a mediumweight hoodie with some nice but cheapfeeling embellishments. The zipper is the worst part  you need to exert a bit of muscle to click the two sides of the zipper teeth together and have them snap before you can move the zipper up. When unzipping you need to jiggle and exert pressure in just the right way to unclasp the last of it. It takes PATIENCE and is frustrating given the price point. When I asked customer care if this is considered a product defect, they said no, all of the [black] jackets are like this and that my options were to take it as or return it. (If it breaks, however, I was told I could call back and return it then; but when I asked about a statue of limitations on such a warranty they said that would be decided on a casebycase basis). The straps around the wrists dont bother me at all as they do some other reviewers. It is warmer than your garden variety hoodie but also less soft. I personally find that the gear on the pockets makes the decoration curl out in a most unflattering way, so the fit around the middle bulkier than I would like (see picture  Im not pregnant anymore and dont want to look it!). Note that this part of the pocket is just decoration  the actual pocket opening is underneath and does not snap shut or anything. I am going to sew this outer part of the pockets shut for a sleeker fit and just keep the item since it is just a hoodie and average is good enough me to to end my hoodie search and endless cycle of Modcloth returns. The Small ended up striking the best balance for me between (baggy enough for) gymwear and (tight enough for) workwear so at least this is versatile. The medium, which I also tried, would have only worked for the gym and felt more like a lightweight winter coat. I am clicking small on the fit because I typically wear an XS.GREEN: The small in this one was too snug (much shorter and a little smaller than the size small in black if Im not mistaken) and really would only have worked as a semicropped cardigan to go with dresses. I sent it back despite the sale price.

review_summary: Review of the Dress for Women with Curves
review_text: I am a woman with curves. That being said, I wanted to write a helpful review for the woman who are over a size 12. I am a size 14 on a good day but usually am a size 16 which is the size of this dress that I am wearing in these pictures. The wedding I am wearing  it to is at the end of May so this is not the finished look that I will be wearing it was just for the sake of trying it on and writing a review. I love the dress but it can be a bit cupcake like on me especially at the waist where it poofs out a little too much (see pics). There are 3 layers of tule on my dress and I really think they could have gotten the same effect with less tule, especially on more curvy women and then with less tule it would be more slimming. The biggest complaint I have though is the neckline although its not a deal breaker. When the dress is on me, it in no way matches the look of the model when it comes to the neckline. There is an awkward scalloped detail along the collar bone and so it does not sit flush against the skin. Whereas on the model, it is perfectly flush along her collarbone. I understand this is most likely because I have more broad shoulders and later breasts however, I think the designer should design and sew it in a way so that it looks very similar on all different kinds of figures. My favorite thing about the dress is the color. This color is exquisite and I really like the lace which makes it look really like a  black tie affair look. I also think the fabric is a nice quality. It is not itchy nor irritating and it is something I could wear all night without being annoyed by the fabric. Finally, the best part about the dress, my breasts are size 36 D and I DO NOT have to wear a bra in order for my girls to stay up and look perky. I think thats awesome because of the fact that if I did wear a normal bra, you would absolutely see the bra straps on this dress. I would recommend this look for curvier women but caution you from thinking that it will fit exactly as it fits on the model. If you purchase it, you have to find a way to make it work on you. I am keeping it and plan to wear it to the wedding in about a month so I will post the pictures of my final look after the wedding!

All of this being said, a past reviewer, Gwendolyn, wondered how to fix a twisted waistband. Ill say if you are comfortable making a cut and sewing it back up its SUPER easy. You need to make a small cut inside the skirt waistband where no one could see and cut the elastic and pull it out altogether. THEN put a safety pin at one end of the elastic and feed it back through your skirt waistband using the safety pin to guide and know where you are in the skirt. Of course being careful you arent twisting it  Once youve made it back around to the slit you cut, sew both the hole and the elastic back in place. I hope that doesnt sound more complicated than it is, I bet there are youtube tutorials on it too. Super easy if you have a needle and thread.

This skirt is kind of nice, but there are definitely some a couple of down points that make me hesitate to keep it. The material itself feels pretty darn cheapits a rough polyester weave, and it shows wrinkles very, very  easily. The details section says to handwash, and I have a sneaking suspicion that if I end up keeping this I will wash it most gingerly indeed, because it does not feel like it will wash well. It might even be worth drycleaning if youre into that kind of thing? The rough weave also makes me worry a little about how well it will wear, since it will show snags or pulls really obviously. The pockets are nice but a bit on the shallower side, so make sure not to put anything too heavy in there!I wear between a US size 8 or 10 in pants, size 6 in dresses, and the size medium juuust fits with enough room to breathe a little. I think a large might have been too big to sit at my natural waist without cinching, though. Its a little dicey getting over the widest part of my hips, but the elastic *will* stretch as long as you leave the belt off or very, very loose; the skirt just slips on, and I found it a bit easier if I gripped more towards the back, where the elastic is (especially if you have any amount of booty).  I wonder a bit if a zipper might not have been a bit easier for putting on and off, but the elastic isnt obnoxious, and it does give it a bit of a more casual feel, which is nice. I am 59, and the skirt hits me about where it does on the model (just below the knee) when sitting at my natural waist, so fellow longerlegged people might enjoy that bonusthats what saves this from three stars! You can see through the fabric a little bit, but only in certain lighting conditions and not enough to see the pattern on your underwear. Because of the aforementioned thinness, I would say that this skirt would be best in spring or summer, but I think itll be fine with thick tights or high socks. The belt is very cheap (still reasonably cute!), but it is removableit feels like its made of the usual vegan leather substitute one sees often, and looks just as plasticky as it really is.The sale price seems about appropriate. Regular price seems a little bit high for what youre getting, honestly.

And this is a highwaisted dress, so the waist is actually hitting at lower ribcage area. After a month or so of debating it I purchased the dress with the support of my three year old nephew! I read the reviews which said the dress was tight around the rib cage and pulled at the chest so I was concerned this dress would not fit me. Im 5 2, 146 lbs. and a 42 DD and ordered a large. The dress fit me perfectly. I was able to slip it over my head without undoing the buttons or the zipper. The fit was loose enough to allow me to wear a slip under the dress. The fabric is a little thinner than I would have liked allowing anything other than a light colored bra to show. The belt that accompanies the dress is a bit thin in width instead I wore a large brown belt that cinched my waist perfectly giving me more of an hour glass figure. The length falls slightly below my knees and suits this retroinspired dress nicely. My only complaint is that once the buttons are loosened they easily pop open without any resistance and had I not been wearing a slip under I could have easily embarrassed myself! However, an easy solution will be to simply sew the buttons as I know I will not have to loosen them to slip the dress on. Im very happy with my purchase as is my nephew who thinks its a pretty yellow dress. I also received so many compliments on the dress that I will definitely be ordering it in some of the other colors!

If you want to impress someone or steal the show, then do wear this dress for an elegant but powerful statement, making you look sweet and pretty, yet also not too girly.

The NotSoGood: the dress material does wrinkle pretty easily, so Id recommend wearing it on a day that youll primarily be standing. The cloth covered buttons, though cute, arent terribly well secured, so you should do as I did and this a couple more stitches into them because it would be a shame to loose them. speaking of the chest region, I am by no means a wellendowed lady in that department, and I cant manage to button up the dress without gaping. In all likelyhood, youre going to have to wear a cami or the like underneath, which isnt really my cup of tea. Overall though, Id still absolutely recommend this dress to a friend. review_text: Ive had this coat for just over a year now, and have worn it spring and fall and some of the (warmer) winter months.  It fits me perfectly and snugly  this means that I cant really fit a heavy sweater underneath so its not suitable for smalltown Southern Ontario winter (and certainly not for Montreal winters!).  I did work one year in Toronto and wore this jacket almost all winter taking public transit.  I like that the collar can stand up against the wind, and that part of it is removable  this makes the jacket very wearable in the spring.  The only negatives about the jacket are: (a) the pockets are VERY shallow.  I lost my iPod nano when it fell out on the subway...so I would not keep anything important in the pockets (not even mitts!), and (b) after about a week, the metal loop on the back of the neck tore off so that I can no longer hang it on a hook off the loop.  Arms are long enough for gangly me (unlike many jackets) and the bust is not too big for my boyish frame.  I wore a backpack most of last year and have not notice any marks on the shoulders (as I do with some jackets)  so the material seems to be durable and good quality.  Im very happy with this jacket!

review_summary: It pains me to write this
review_text: It pains me to write this, as these jeans are absolutely perfect when first tried on, but after having bought several pairs Ive come to some unfortunate conclusions. These are not the same Karaoke Songstress jeans that were originally found on ModCloth. While theyre still made by Judy Blue, the fabric content has changed. Theyve become stretchier which is good  for minimal wear, but they have no durability whatsoever. Of the three pairs Ive either purchased or received as gifts, none has resisted stretching. Within a month or two of regular wear, the fabric begins to stretch out around my crotch and upper thighs, leaving a very unflattering pouch of fabric. This has occurred whether Ive hand washed, washed on delicate in the machine and hung to dry, or allowed it to dry in the dryer to try and shrink them back into shape. The bottom line is that if you only wear jeans occasionally, or are curvy enough that this sort of stretch is necessary, go for it. They are the perfect rise, theyre comfy, and theyre very flattering. Just dont expect them to last. And for girls who wear jeans often, save yourself the heartbreak and cash and invest in a higher quality pair with a lower spandex content. Youll thank me, I promise.

This dress is growing on me. The belt, as others have noted, is junk. However, its easy to swap in something that fits and is higher quality, and since I own a couple already, Im not annoyed by the extra cost of replacing this one. The beltloops themselves are nice and thick, but you could remove them if you didnt want to get a different belt. As for the rest of the dress, there are a lot of pros. Its not lined, but the fabric is heavy and flows nicely. The tailoring is decent, although the pleats in the back dont lie exactly as they should (I think the zipper was slightly mislayed). Overall, Id say my Cue The Compliments dress is far superior in quality (for less $$), but its hard to wear a bright red dress all the time and this purple Luck Be A Lady adds some nice variation to my wardrobe. It can be styled quite easily  so far I like it with either the Dream of the Crop Cardigan in navy or the Black Tea with Milk Top (please excuse the bedhead in the picture)  and while it is shorter than expected, its not too short for work if you wear tights (a must for Canadian winters anyway). Its also very comfortable  I wear dresses all the time, and thanks to the elastic, this one is very easy to move in.The 12 fit perfectly, even in the chest (which can be an issue with my small bust). Overall I think I will get a lot of wear out of this from fall through spring (it is too heavy for summer), and Id buy another in the same style if they offered a pattern I liked.

So I contact modcloth, got them to exchange it (the exchange policy on this website is really nice), and waited for the new ones to come in.  When they finally arrived, I was so excited to finally get the jeans of my dreams, and they fit perfectly.  I wore them out one day and was so happy with how they fit. But when I went home I noticed that one of the small metal buttonattachment things by the pocket had come of *before Id even put them on* I noticed the 2 pieces to it sitting by the container it had come in.  Part of me wanted to exchange it again, but I figured out a way to glue it back on so it stays on through the wash, and I dont think Ill exchange them again. So I guess I just wanted to leave this review to let anybody else who wants these jeans that they are very cute, but that they are also pretty low quality considering the price.

I love this sweater! Its my first Christmas sweater, ever, and its just amazing. It arrived two day early, just in time for me to never take it off until after Christmas! Its thinner than I imagined, and more along the lines of a boyfriend fit. But the roominess of it makes it undeniably comfortable. Im an inbetweener in sizing: Not quite a large, and not quite a medium on ModCloth. Despite my measurements, I come across as generally petite in most sections, save my tummy, and so my waist naturally sucks in the some of the extra baggage of the sweater, which makes it almost flattering on me (its a Christmas sweater, remember?). If youre after this for a fashionable fit, Id order a size down, and keep in mind that it wasnt knit to flatter! Ive gotten so many compliments on it all day, and countless laughs and highfives from fans of the movie. The cotton content allows for breathability, while the acrylic will keep this baby from wearing down after the washes. Im not sure why they called it intarsia, as it looks to me more like double knitting on the front panel and sleeves. This means that the parts with color work on it (the Leg Lamp, snow, etc) are twice as thick as the sleeve cuffs and back panel, which is nice, considering the thinness of yarn used. Technical jargon aside, this is a highquality knit sweater that Im sure will become almost as legendary a Christmas piece as the movie that inspired it. :)

I am one of those people who adores October because of Halloween, and celebrate all month long. I have some festive tshirts, but have been looking for a sweater for the month, so when I found this, I completely fell in love! The design is so cute, and since its a Modcloth Intarsia sweater, I knew its be a decently thick, knitted fabric. The Intarsia Modcloth line is my favorite, and Ive already purchased several from the collection, but to those who havent: these sweaters run SMALL, I am normally a size M or even a size S for oversized sweaters, but these have a more flattering cut than a normal sweatshirt, so they do cling a bit. Also, the Intarsia sweater line is meant to have 3/4 sleeves that end above your wrist; Im only five feet tall, so they are like normal sleeves for me, but if you are taller or have longer arms, they will be shorter, because they are meant to be. I see a lot of reviews complaining about this, when it is shown in the picture they are meant to be shorter, so be aware of that. Overall, this is probably my favorite sweater in my entire wardrobe, and as long as you are aware of how this sweater fits (smaller, shorter sleeves), then I HIGHLY recommend it!

Ohhhh the never ending saga of me and this coat! This is the third fall/winter Ive tried to own it. Third time lucky?! The first year I just discovered Modcloth as it sold out. Last year I jumped on the L as soon as it came in, but it was too tight in an odd area  below the shoulders but above the fullest part of the bust. The XL was sold out, so I tried the 1X but that was just wishful thinking. I reluctantly sent them both back and the XL was never restocked. This year I snatched up the XL as soon as it was listed, certain that this would finally be the perfect fit, but... its like a tent on me. Bigger than last years 1X. I can work the Paddington Bear look if I must, but I was hoping for something slightly more fitted. Its clear that the measurements vary from year to year on this piece  as evidenced by the photos of 54 ladies where the coat just hits the hips. Im 510 and have a long torso, but the XL I was sent this year comes right past my butt. Im holding on to it while I order the L and will just keep whichever of the two looks the best. I agree with everyone that the sleeves are short, but I love the crafty solution proposed by reviewer Antonia: sewing in legwarmers! I might even knit some cuffs in a luxurious wool. Aside from fit issues, this coat is GORGEOUS: huge hood, rich and unique burnt orange colour, roomy pockets and sturdy medium weight fabric perfect for fall layering. Clearly it keeps me coming back :)

review_text: I bought this dress to wear to a wedding this summer and was SO pleased with the fit and look of this dress.  Ive worn it to church a few times since and always get so many compliments. This dress fit the bill perfectly.  Like other reviewers have mentioned, it is on the thin side (I feel more comfortable wearing a half slip underneath, but its probably not necessary for everyone...Id just rather err on the side of modesty) and it does wrinkle quite easily, but thats nothing a little starch wont take care of.  Overall, I love this dress.  And this being my first purchase with ModCloth, I have to  mention how impressed I was with their customer service.  I got advise from the ModCloth stylists about styling this dress for the wedding and they did a brilliant job and really made me feel comfortable and confident about my outfit which is the most important part of looking great.

Despite that, it does look really nice when open and freeflowing! Unfortunately, I dont find the quality of the fabric to be so high. The outside is nice when you run your hand on it, but the inside was vaguely itchy against my bare skin. The zipper is also kind of tricky since the fabric is very lightweight. Lastly, one of the stitches was loose and fraying when it arrived. Overall, I think the look is in principle really cool, and I can imagine that this would look nicer on someone with a slimmer figure (or maybe better on me if I got one size larger). Sadly, I think Im going to return it ultimately because I just dont find the quality up to par.

Im a clothing designer and seamstress...when something fits weird, it REALLY bugs me. So, here are my two biggest issues with this jacket  Ill let you decide for yourself if its worth the $55 + tax and shipping.1) I ordered a Small, and despite being fairly true to size in all other proportions, the fit in the shoulders and armholes was off by enough that I not only noticed it, but couldnt keep wearing it because it bothered me so much. The armholes are cut improperly, which feels really awkward when worn, like my shoulders are being forced back because theres not enough room in the front of the armscye and too much in the back. I was tempted to rip the sleeves out and recut the armscye myself, but thats opening a whole other can of worms and Id rather just order a size Medium and see if the fit across the shoulders doesnt improve when I go up a size.2) The quality of the material is not as nice as I would have expected for something of this price. The trouble is that this jacket has a synthetic type of jersey knit that makes me worry that its going to start pilling anywhere theres friction (under the arms mainly). Sure it looks nice when you pull it out of the bag, but check the armpits after a month of regular wear and tell me its not pill city under there. Since fit and quality are my two most important expectations from a garment, Im sad to say this jacket did not deliver on either account so its going back.

If you have long hair, it will tangle in the zipper with the hood out. And it looks rather stupid if you man auto get the hood zipped inNext we will look at pockets. There are 2 pockets only. The zippers in the chest are pure decorations (useless) the two normal pockets that LOOK like they close up do NOT. There is literally a flap with a functioning pop button that is attached to the outer flap for the illusion of securing your stuff in your pocket Okay now, the sleeves. What were you thinking? There is an extra strap that looks like it will help to close the sleeves up to keep the cold air from getting in. It doesnt. All it does is create an odd triple layered bulky wrist issue. review_text: On one hand, the last thing I needed was a hoodie, but on the other, I thought this was the perfect replacement for the faded black hoodie I had loved for so long. One of my least favorite things is having cuffs that stretch out long before the garment is ready to go, and I do not have that fear with the way this is constructed.I like enough that I will likely order another one in the near future.

I was not happy with the fit, but I gathered it with a safety pin and it looked okay. I read reviews saying that the midriff part was too big or the top was small and the skirt was big and weird. Yet, no one mentioned the key fix! After I took the dress off and put it on a hanger, I noticed there is actually a belt loop on the front inside part of the skirt. It doesnt show it in the model photo, but its there. All you have to do is put the top ties through it and it keeps the skirt up and the midriff from showing too much. Its functional and looks even cuter that way. I like the length of the dress because it hits just above my knees and overall Im pretty happy!

review_summary: I want to start by saying
review_text: I want to start by saying Ive bought these twice, and this is a review having worn them out, not like most reviews which give you an idea how it is straight out of the box. Fit? Lovely. So if your thighs rub, thats where it will fall apart first. Mine also rubbed thin around the ankles, which is something Ive only seen in jeans Ive owned for years. Stretchy fabrics like this tend to be less durable anyway, though, so maybe I just cant have my cake and eat it too.Ive also purchased them in black, and that one was a different brand. That one had slightly thicker material and lasted more like six months. So, overall Ive owned three pairs of Sleeks for Itself pants, and none of them had much longevity. But for $40 youll look good and feel good for ten weeks.

After doing an indepth research study of these pants, I think I finally figured them out.  Someone said in another review that they are basically high waisted jeggings, and they are right.  If you order your size (which I did at first), they will fit you like a glove and hold in any pudge you might have, and make you look totally hot.  However, you might sacrifice a little comfort if you do this, having compacted all your flesh into a sausage casing, and there might be some bunching in places where the material is overstretched or looser than in other places.  I decided to order the 13s to see the difference because on me, a tall girl, the legs on the 11s bunched up a little too much, and they were on the short side in lenght.  When I got the 13s, I found that they were a little bit longer, (covering my ankle bone when standing), and didnt ride up my legs as much, as a result of having a little more room.  Also, they were truly high waisted on me, which wasnt the case on the 11s.  They didnt fit me like a glove in the butt and hips, however, and I can see how I might want to take them in at the waist if they stretch out a little.  Anyway, I decided to keep the 13s for the length and the extra room, sacrificing that legging look from the 11s.  The 13s are more like skinny jeans with a little room.  I could also see how you could order two sizes up in these and they would look like really comfy, stretchy jeans.

Very versatile, flattering dress! I had trouble deciding whether to buy the S or M, but ended up getting the M. I usually wear a size 4 or S dress, but with MC dresses I often have to size up to get them to fit my bust. In this case, the M fits just fine in the bust and is loose and floaty around the hips, so it was the right decision. The waist hits a bit high on me, which is usually unattractive because I have a wide ribcage, but in this case it still looks great. The style is slimming and so very flattering. I really think MC has found the universally flattering dress style! It shows off a small bust, flatters a large bust, and hides larger hips if thats a problem area for you. The neckline is lovely, and the little cap sleeves slim your arms. Its not a short as many MC dresses, so it could be worn when a mini isnt appropriate. Because I got the M, it is actually a bit longer than I wanted (covers my knees), but Im only 5 tall so that will not be a problem for most people. The only thing that might not be flattering on everyone is the color. I like the olive green (its a bit greener thant it appeared on the website), but im not sure if it would look good on all skintones. I hope MC carries this dress in more colors, because Id definitely buy more!

My boyfriend gifted me this jacket. It looks cute but I had an issue with the zipper getting off track within 2 weeks of buying it. He was able to fix it by using pliers to take the stops off the zipper end but overall the quality of this jacket is not very high. The fabric is not lined and the interior is somewhat rough, almost like terry cloth. The outside looks smooth and cute, though. The hood, as others have said, is tricky to get back in the collar (I can do it fairly easily by rolling it up first but I DO worry about the zipper holding up every time I do it). My biggest peeve is that the drawstrings dont affect the hood whatsoever! Its only for the collar (which is pretty useless). So if you want a hood to not blow off your head or have any sort of fitted aspect when youre walking outside, this will not do it. I really just keep the hood inside all the time which makes the collar rather heavy/bulky. The sleeve cuffs are unnecessarily thick and heavy as well and dont keep your wrists very warm as you cant put your hands in the pockets without a gap. Overall, if I had tried this on in person I would not have bought it. As a gift, and to wear in mid40s to low 50s weather, its acceptable.

I still have to pull them up a bit when I stand up from sitting, but otherwise, they fit without looking like theyve been painted on me. The quality is okay. Decent for the price. review_text: The small was too snug for me to be comfortable. The medium is a bit too big, but that just means that it sits below the natural waist on me. However, with both sizes, the waist band did not sit flat against my body like it does on the product photo; it stuck straight up, gapping away from me. I read only a few other reviews with this issue, so I imagine its not common. Ill have to have it tailored, but my interim solution has been to wear a wide black belt over the waistband to disguise the gap. This will work fine until I want to wear the skirt with a top untucked. The quality is high  very thick fabric with straight seams and no loose threads. When I first washed the skirt (by hand in cold water with Woolite), it bled quite a lot, so do be careful if you choose to machine wash this with other garments.The skirt does pick up lint pretty easily, so be aware of that if you have pets or work in a dusty environment. Also, when I ordered the skirt, I thought that the second layer at the bottom was only partial; both layers are the full length of the skirt (minus the 1 or 2 inch difference at the bottom), which meet at the waistband. This does make it a bit more difficult to iron, and also makes the skirt quite heavy. Its a stiff fabric, not flowy, so Im really not sure why both layers are the full length... but I like the skirt regardless. Overall a great purchase, well worth the price. review_text: Ive been a fan of Mod Cloth for years and have always wanted the Coach Tour dress, but never purchased it. First off, this dress is darling.  As many before me have said, the pictures are beautiful and it is unsurprisingly even more gorgeous in person.  I normally wear and ordered a 2. The dress had a nice, tight fit, but I couldnt zip the dress on my own. I sized up to a 4 which was more comfortable but still appeared tight.As several have said, the lace top and sleeves are a bit itchy.  I have very sensitive skin but it wasnt a problem for me.  The bodice and skirt are lined with a lovely silky material, so no itch there. The silky skirt clings so be prepared to deal with that one way or another. The high waisted skirt does make me feel a little selfconscious and poofy, but worrying is all for naught because it looks great on. I love how it hits the midcalf of most girls who have posted photos here, however it was a bit short on me, coming just below the knee.My dealbreaker is that the tulle DOES provide stretch, but not in the direction that anyone wants.  The tulle stretches if (gently!) pulled vertically, but not horizontally.  This means that there is no room to breathe since the bodice doesnt give any.  It also makes this dress a nightmare to try to get into and out of.  The only way I can get out of this dress on my own is to unzip, bend over, and slowly and gently pull the back of the skirt over my head, thus slowly turning the dress inside out. Painful and not very dignified!Ill try my luck with the longer one that is available in March!

review_summary: Fit is a bit odd, but I love this dress!!
review_text: I LOVE THIS DRESS. The color is a little less yellow in person, and I think it actually compliments my pale, pinkish complexion without washing me out (which is a miracle in and of itself). The narrow straps and waistline are not a problem, which I thought they would with my broad shoulders, largeish bust, and long waist. It is so flattering that I did not want to take it off. Part of me really wants to buy the navy blue one, too, even though its very similar to the Here Comes the Stride Midi Dress in Midnight dress that I already have. Even if I dont use this as a wedding dress (which I probably will), I plan on keeping it! Having said all of that, there are some odd points. 1. There are builtin cups which are incredibly obvious. These may have to be removed during alterations. 2. The sizing is weird. Initially I purchased an 18, since it was the closest to my size that was still in stock. This surprisingly fit very well, even though Im actually between a 12 and 14 in this brand. When a 14 came in, it was only a little smaller than the 18. I dont know if the 18 is really a mismarked 16 or if there are just really subtle differences between the sizes. 3. The bust is too big. This is just a matter of tailoring, but I was disappointed to see Id have to take a good inch or two off of the bust and waist to make it work to its fullest potential. Im tempted to try a 12 if it becomes available, but when Ive tried that in other Chi Chi London dresses, I cant zip it up. Theres something weird with their sizing.4. The dress weight makes the straps dig into my shoulders. I anticipate this is because the bodice is not fitting more tightly, but it is a bit of a nuisance. I still love the dress even with those (admittedly small) negatives. Theres a lot of thought that went into this dress design, even down to lining the inside with a silky fabric so nothing is scratchy. I definitely recommend it, and I encourage Modcloth to not only restock all of the sizes but also to get a larger size model showing this dress off, because it can be stunning with curves!

review_summary: So, I switch between an X
review_text: So, I switch between an XL and a 1X in Modcloth sizing, and after reading the reviews, was fairly happy with purchasing these in 1X.  There is a *lot* of spandex in these, compared to other stretch denim Ive owned, which is a mixed blessing.  On the one hand, they are very forgiving if youre packing a lot of junk in your trunk.  On the other, they tend to loosen and wiggle down over the course of the day.  One thing I find irksome is that the pockets are not welllined  the denim just barely dips into the front pocket, and so when the jeans wiggle down, the linings start to show and I find it unsightly.  Im considering just taking a bit of thread and tacking the front pockets shut, as the jeans are otherwise flattering despite their flaws.

It is also very easy to iron; however, the button on the sleeve does not come undone, so youll have to be a little more diligent with your iron. After the first pressing, though, its remained wrinkle free through multiple wears! Makes getting dressed quick and easy. The tunic is slightly see through; however, if you have neutral/skin tone undergarments, no one can tell.I paired this tunic two ways. The length of this shirt landed an inch aboveboard my knee, so I was able to wear it a dress. If you were to do so, I suggest loosening the sash, as when you raise your arms, the tunic travels with you. With leggings, the sash can be tied as loose or as tight as you desire (I prefer a more form fitting appearance, so I keep it tight with leggings). Its a little bulky with jeans. The length of the tunic looks odd tucked in or left flowing, but Ive found that high waisted anything with just the front tucked in and the back left out looks really cute. I highly recommend this if you want comfort and style in one. Easy to dress up or dress down, and therefore perfect for someone like myself!

review_text: This is my very first Modcloth purchase. I am happy. It is almost as if this coat was made for me. I am normally an XL in everything I buy except coats. It pulls slightly across the chest but If I wear a different bra this fixes the problem. It leaves me a bit of extra length in the arms. It come to my knuckles.I dont love the buttons, they are a lil more ball like then I thought. Easy enough to change if I really wanted. I can see it pilling with wear but I have only had it a few hours so I cant say for sure. I paid 41.19 on top of shipping. Which seemed a little steep to Calgary, Alberta, Canada. I wonder if that would have been different had I not used UPS?All in all I paid almost 200 Canadian for this coat. It is a beautiful coat and I might have even spent that in store for it. Just be aware of the extra rate when purchasing outside of the USA. That alone will probably stop me from buying too much form this site. I bought this dress for my wedding (another year away) and I am so excited about it! Im short and curvy, so I was looking for a kneelength vintage dress, be comfortable to wear, suit a Fall Wedding, and was under $200. This dress hit all the check marks, and I got it during one of the sales (win!)I was worried being such a low price, that the fabric would be a little cheap looking or the dress poorly made. But when I opened it, I was really excited to see how delicate and ornate the details were! The bottom half of the gown is really lovely, the top is flattering but conservative, and the side zipper really helps getting the dress on/off. It also has builtin bra pads (which I missed in the info description) so thats a win! I dont think Ill end up needing to wear a bra under the dress which was a concern I had. I only have a few notes to share that I consider really minor and easy to fix: theres 3 layers of tool between the dress and the slip, so it jets out a little more than I like (my hips are about 38, plus poofy dress). Im considering removing at least one layer to calm it down, but I have a lot of time between now and my wedding so I might change my mind. A frequent note in other reviews is that the top neckline lace work near the collar bone sometimes folds in on its self, which I also experienced. A little fabric tape would do the trick though.Overall, Im really happy with this dress and I cant wait to wear it for real!

review_summary: First of all this is a be
review_text: First of all this is a beautiful coat. The ruby color is lovely, and the quality of the coat is top notch. Unfortunately, the fit just didnt work for me. I am normally a Small, but that was sold out, so I tried the Medium. As soon as I slipped it on I thought the Medium would be perfect because it was slightly snug in the shoulders, and I only had a light shirt on  not a bulky sweater. But when I went to button the coat I realized it was just too big overall. I tied the belt to see if that masked the size issue but it didnt. For me, the appeal of this coat was not only the style and color, but also how it comes in nicely to highlight the waist. In my case the Medium doesnt do this, and the Small will likely be too tight in the shoulders. Sadly, this beautiful coat is going right back.

review_summary: I had been eyeing these j
review_text: I had been eyeing these jeans for a long time and finally got them. They have great reviews so I feel strange being the only way to not give them amazing praise and wonder now if it was just the ones I got...but I have to say, although cute on, these are not the best quality jeans at all. Right out of the bag I found them to be very thin, thinner than any other pair of jeans I have. I also noticed stitching sticking out on the leg. When I went to try them on with the cuffs rolled up I also noticed a goopy substance, like black die maybe, on the inside of the jeans. It rubbed off on me and wont come off the jeans. I am hoping with a wash on cold it will go away but for $60 still very disappointing.  The fit is great, especially since having a child my body has changed so much I have thick thighs and calves and a smaller sized waist and these fit the bill for that, including cover my postbaby belly poof. I normally wear an 8 in jeans so I got a 9 which is good.The fit is good overall and after ordering and returning another item and then ordering these and waiting for them (over a month worth of time!) I am super reluctant to return them. I will keep them but I do feel that for the price these are disappointing, to say the least, in quality. :(

review_text: I bought this skirt as a wildcard in an outfit I was trying to put together, not really expecting that it would work. review_summary: I wanted these to work so
review_text: I wanted these to work so bad and I was so disappointed in the reality of tunics. I bought them in almost every color because they are so perfect for virtually every scenario, but they are so cheaply made that Ive had an identical tear in more than two of them. They are not made of a stretchy material, but if you put any pressure at all on the seams surrounding the buttons its just straight up tears. Its not that these are too small or constantly of pressure on them, but for the occasion where you are reaching something or using your shoulders in a way that stretches the center it doesnt even have any give. The material is some kind of synthetic polyester I believe so when it tears it basically frays into a bunch of tiny little threads and I just dont see how I can fix it without it looking poorly done. I will fix them anyway but considering the spot and the lack of extra fabric its gonna look very clearly taped or glued. They should not be $40 if they are going to tear in the first three uses. I am a diehard ModCloth shopper partly because they have such good customer service and respond so well to the situations but theres nothing they can do about this one. I usually wear a M in MC tops/sweaters, but tried this in the S and Im glad I did. I really like it, and the S fits with room to spare. The sleeves and the length of the sweater are fine also. Its a swing style, but not too full. I have a short neck, so I probably would not wear the collar buttoned all the way up, but I can button it and then scrunch it down and it looks fine. It can also be worn open (with the collar spread out like a blazer), or with just the second button buttoned. I attached some photos of different ways I tried the collar. The color is a nice deep gray that is very versatile, and the weight is good for fall/winter here in the South. The only negatives in my opinion are the shape of the sleeves (I wish they were straighter and not so flared at the hem), and I wish it had pockets! I also wish it was a natural fiber, and thats why I gave it 4 stars instead of 5. I would recommend sizing down if you are petite or if  you have a slim torso and shoulders. Overall Im very pleased that I took a chance on this one and cant wait for cooler weather so I can wear it.

review_summary: I had been looking for a
review_text: I had been looking for a red sweater for a long time when I saw this one. The material is soft and really comfortable, and the red is a nice deep red, and it was exactly what I had been searching for!  But seriously, size up.

Aside from the sizing issue, the color is lovely and the ruffles are adorable without feeling childish. The sleeves do not feel long enough but I expected this due to my height.  For reference, i typically wear XL/1X (16/18) in tops but 2X (18/20) in bottoms.

review_summary: I tried this on at the Mo
review_text: I tried this on at the Modcloth shop. Its super cute in person. I had real issues with the sizing though. The difference between an L and an XL is comical. The XL was huge and extremely unflattering. Its not fitted and it doesnt come in at the waist at all. It looked like a giant sack. As I tend to be an XL in jackets I was surprised. So I tried the L. It was cut beautifully, flattering tailoring but *much* smaller. While the XL swam on me, the L was so tight across my bust I couldnt zip it all the way up. I have a larger chest, so its not a new problem, but the difference in size and cut blew me away. I found the color and feel of the material slightly different on the XL too. I would recommend this if youre looking for a size L or below. But the cut and quality are not replicated in the larger sizes. A real shame as it is very cute.

Another commenter said having the dress professionally pressed to help with the poofiness was also effective. I found the color to be a true champagne, not a shiny gold as others have suggested. I think its very true to the online photos. This was the first dress I tried on, and I was immediately sold! Its exactly what I wanted.

I confess, I didnt measure what a 34.5 length would be on me, so the dress was borderline scandalous instead of cute.  Judging by others pictures, I thought it would hit just shy of my knees, but it was definitely midthigh.  In the size L, I found the ascot collar more awkward than pictured, as the buttoned part of the collar doesnt stretch all the way across the shoulder in the larger size.  I also thought the collar was substantially less full compared to the picture.  I agree with previous reviewers who have commented about the pockets: they are adorable, yes, but if you have fuller hips, they may hit at an unfortunate height.  I looked tiny and fey from the ribcage up, but my lower half simply exploded.  My hips jutted the dress out into a very abrupt triangle, which detracted from the dress overall simplicity.  In person, the buttons are VERY coppery, so plan your metallic accessories accordingly. While I wish I could keep this, it wasnt a good fit on my body type.  The quality was strong, and the material very comfortable.  This would be a perfect dress to wear on a long flight: soft, warm, wrinklefree!

review_text: I ADORE this skirt. Im super picky about my skirts, especially as someone with long legs and a tendency to sit with legs splayed. I bought it for work, because my slacks were getting worn too quickly, and I literally wear this skirt day after day. My only warning is that the skirt IS quite long. I am 58, with decently long legs, and the skirt hits just below my knees. However, it is literally a circleskirt, so if youre a hand with a sewing machine, a little basting will tuck it up nicely. Run an iron over the seams, and the fabric will keep the hem for a good long time. I was surprised, when I opened it, by the fabric. I expected something softer and heavier, like a twill. The polyester is fairly stiff, and I was worried that it would feel cheap. Turns out, though, that because of the stiffness of the polyester, the skirt keeps its body wonderfully, and it still has that marvelous pooling effect when you sit down. It also doesnt wrinkle easily, which is wonderful, and seems pretty stain resistant. I can wear this skirt four days in a row, just running a lint roller over it, and no one would know I hadnt washed it. And it totally flares when you spin! 10/10 would buy again.
